name: Illinois

localAgencies.name: Cook County Department of Environment and Sustainability
localAgencies.notes: Requires equipment registration permits for air emission equipment (even units Illinois EPA treats as insignificant) under Cook County Code §§ 30-151 and 32-1. This is in addition to Illinois EPA permits.

localAgencies.name: City of Chicago Department of Public Health
localAgencies.notes: Issues city air pollution control permits.

overview: Illinois EPA requires a construction permit before building an emission unit or air pollution control equipment unless an exemption applies, and an operating permit to operate. Operating permit options depend on size: Registration of Smaller Sources (ROSS) for very small sources, lifetime state operating permits, general permits for true minor sources, FESOPs for synthetic minors, and CAAPP (Illinois's Title V program) for major sources. PSD and nonattainment NSR apply to major projects.

permitTypes.name: Permit exemptions
permitTypes.description: Appendix 2 / Section 201.146 lists equipment and activities that need no construction or operating permit (e.g., certain small combustion units, storage tanks, cold cleaning degreasers). Exempt units must still meet other requirements and can count toward NSR or CAAPP applicability.

permitTypes.name: Registration of Smaller Sources (ROSS)
permitTypes.description: Registration replaces a permit for eligible small sources, based on prior-year actual emissions from non-exempt units. Annual fee applies.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per Illinois EPA guide: up to 5.0 tons/yr combined PM, CO, NOx, SO2, and VOM; 0.50 tons/yr combined HAPs; 0.05 tons/yr lead; 0.05 tons/yr mercury.

permitTypes.name: Construction Permit
permitTypes.description: Required before building an emission unit or air pollution control equipment, or making a modification, unless exempt.

permitTypes.name: Lifetime State Operating Permit
permitTypes.description: Operating permit for non-CAAPP, non-FESOP sources that does not require renewal unless the Agency requests it.
permitTypes.citation: Ill. Environmental Protection Act; 35 Ill. Adm. Code 201

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: Available only to true minor sources; allow adding or modifying units within the permit's limits without a new construction permit. Illinois EPA has also issued general FESOPs (e.g., batch-mix asphalt).

permitTypes.name: Federally Enforceable State Operating Permit (FESOP)
permitTypes.description: Voluntary synthetic minor permit with federally enforceable limits keeping potential emissions below major source thresholds.

permitTypes.name: PSD
permitTypes.description: Major source review in attainment areas.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per Illinois EPA guide: 100 tons/yr for 28 listed source categories; 250 tons/yr for others.

permitTypes.name: Nonattainment New Source Review
permitTypes.description: Major source review in nonattainment areas.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per Illinois EPA guide: 100 tons/yr in a nonattainment area (lower thresholds may apply depending on classification).

permitTypes.name: Clean Air Act Permit Program (CAAPP)
permitTypes.description: Illinois's Title V program for major sources and certain other sources.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per Illinois EPA guide: 100 tons/yr of any criteria pollutant; 10 tons/yr of any single HAP; 25 tons/yr of combined HAPs (potential to emit at 8,760 hours/yr).

oilAndGas.summary: Illinois EPA's permitting pages list no oil-and-gas-specific air permit. Oil and gas facilities follow construction, lifetime, FESOP, or CAAPP permitting; federal NSPS OOOO-series and NESHAP HH apply where applicable.

notes: The Illinois EPA eligibility guide is dated 2016; fee amounts and ROSS deadlines in it may be outdated. The Chicago-area ozone nonattainment classification can lower major source thresholds; check the Green Book.
